LESSON: LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: LISTENING comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about LISTENING comprehension. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Solve simple riddles in and out of school.
2. Sing songs with actions in and out of school. language puzzles.
3. Recite poems and rhymes with actions in and out of school. with actions. e) Take pleasure in activities that involve digital comics and answer simple listening for questions. comprehension. simple riddles. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, critical and creative thinking for problem solving, learning to learn, and digital literacy.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Solve simple riddles in and out of school.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to solve simple riddles in and out of school. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Sing songs with actions in and out of school. language puzzles.

3. Recite poems and rhymes with actions in and out of school. with actions. e) Take pleasure in activities that involve digital comics and answer simple listening for questions. comprehension. simple riddles. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, critical and creative thinking for problem solving, learning to learn, and digital literacy.

Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, critical and creative thinking for problem solving, learning to learn, and digital literacy. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about LISTENING comprehension.
2. Explain LISTENING comprehension to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand LISTENING comprehension.
4. Show that you can: Solve simple riddles in and out of school.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about LISTENING comprehension. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is LISTENING comprehension important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Solve simple riddles in and out of school.
2. Sing songs with actions in and out of school. language puzzles.
3. Core-competence developed: Communication and collaboration, critical and creative thinking for problem solving, learning to learn, and digital literacy.
